text:
maya: Quick thread — we need a principled way to prioritize the preflight queue. heavy models (large params / long seqs) are starving light models in the current FIFO.

sam: +1. Seen customer-facing latency because a single full-microbench run locks a GPU pool for 10+ mins.

raj: can we do weighted slots? small quick probes get higher concurrency, heavy probes get reserved singletons with a cost-estimate?

luis: happy path: fast probes (smoke, kv-check, simple perf) should be fast and cheap. full microbench is expensive and can be scheduled off-peak or on dedicated hosts.

maya: sketch of priority queue config I had in mind:

```
queue:
  - name: "fast_prober"
    priority: 100
    weight: 5    # proportional concurrency
    max_runtime_s: 45
  - name: "medium_smoke"
    priority: 70
    weight: 2
    max_runtime_s: 300
  - name: "full_microbench"
    priority: 10
    weight: 1
    max_runtime_s: 1800
```

maya: key ideas:
- use a token-budget signal (est. GPU-seconds) from the ingest metadata to route to a queue
- let orgs set per-customer budget caps so large internal teams don't starve others
- allow opportunistic packing: if no heavy jobs, allow full_microbench to run on fast_prober slots with grace period

sam: how do we get the "est. GPU-seconds" cheaply? model size + peak-seq-len is rough but works. also quantization mode affects runtime (int8 vs fp16).

raj: we can use the analyzer that runs at upload time to produce a small cost vector. keep it simple: {params_m, peak_seq, quant_mode}. validator writes it to model metadata.

ana: scheduler-bot: Added support for metadata-based routing in the staging scheduler. you can opt-in via flag `--routing-by-cost`.

luis: what about fairness? priority weighting could be gamed by flipping flags. need a circuit-breaker: if an org exceeds daily GPU-seconds, demote their queue to best-effort.

maya: agree. propose soft quotas + overage throttles + alerting. quotas enforced in admission, with a manual override path for platform eng.

sam: another thing — golden-input sampling: we should reserve a small set of golden prompts that always run on heavy models but only a tiny fraction of tokens to detect regressions quickly. cheap but high-signal.

maya: yes — golden probes run inside fast_prober even for heavy models, before full_microbench. if golden fails, block rollout.

raj: curious about preemption: should a queued heavy job be preempted mid-run if a P0 smoke needs the capacity? preemption is messy (KV cache lost). maybe only preempt queued, not running.

luis: agree — only preempt waiting jobs. running jobs get best-effort completion. add checkpointing for long microbenchers so partial results still useful.

maya: operational hooks:
- per-queue dashboards (latency, wait-time, GPU-seconds consumed)
- per-org spend and throttle alerts
- canary mode: new routing canary for a subset of models/orgs for 48h

sam: implementation plan: 2-week spike to add cost metadata + routing policy in staging, wire scheduler-bot flag, and add golden probe runner. then gradual rollout.

raj: tests: fuzz routing with synthetic models (weights 10x) and make sure fast_prober tail latency < 200ms for smoke checks in 95th.

maya: small nits: name queues clearly, don't use "fast" vs "full" in UI (confusing). use labels: smoke, medium, full-bench.

scheduler-bot: scheduled test run: model-543 queued to fast_prober (priority 100).

ana: +1 on naming, will add UI labels.

luis: are we okay with golden inputs living in repo or per-customer? probably per-customer golden set for enterprise, global golden set for platform-level regressions.

maya: decision summary:
- implement priority queues with weight-based concurrency
- add cheap cost-estimate metadata at ingest (params, seq, quant)
- run golden probes in fast queue for heavy models before scheduling full microbench
- enforce soft per-org quotas and throttle with alerts
- spike in staging for 2 weeks, then canary rollout

ana: I'll create the spike ticket + rough milestones. assigning to @sam and @maya.

sam: I'll own the scheduler changes, ping me for infra.

maya: I'll own the metadata analyzer and golden probe harness.

raj: thanks all — this should cut the noisy tail and improve onboarding latency for small models. :thumbsup:
